page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processors operating at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 extensions including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, AES, and SHA encryption instructions. The platform includes 768.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio.

Storage architecture is defined by 23,038 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, providing direct high-throughput local disk storage alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The system features no bundled GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. In memory throughput testing, the server achieved 229.38 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 140.83 GB/sec in large-block write operations, reflecting consistent large-footprint data transfer rates.

Benchmark measurements position the L96as_v4 in the top tier for compute-intensive and I/O-bound workloads. It registered 147,596.42 in stress-ng multi-core testing and 22,976.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Data-centric metrics include 122.77 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a PassMark database score of 27,642.68. Compiler workloads reached 66,021.0 on Clang software compilation tests. While single-threaded compression and decompression perform at average rates, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 547.27 GB/sec.

With its combination of dense NVMe storage, high multi-core throughput, and substantial memory capacity, the instance offers balanced resource efficiency for scaled architectures without requiring distributed nodes. The hardware configuration fits high-throughput transactional and analytical databases, large distributed NoSQL engines, search indexing clusters, and intensive data processing pipelines.

Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is structured for I/O-intensive workloads including high-scale NoSQL databases, transactional engines, big data analytics, and search index operations.
